key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum computers can simulate atomic nuclei using adapted nuclear Hamiltonians, with resource costs that are already competitive for some shell-model cases but much higher for no-core-shell models.
engineering_relevance: It provides the first Toffoli and qubit resource estimates for nuclear quantum simulation, helping engineers gauge when nuclear applications may become practical on future fault-tolerant hardware.
method: Constructs quantum algorithms for nuclear structure using effective shell-model Hamiltonians.
Extends the approach to no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians with three-body interactions from chiral effective field theory.
Compiles the algorithms and estimates Toffoli gate and qubit requirements for representative nuclei.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resource estimates for $^{32}$Mg and $^{219}$At shell-model Hamiltonians that are comparable to recent Femoco chemistry benchmarks, while no-core-shell-model cases for light nuclei require substantially more resources.
watch_item: The no-core-shell-model simulations appear far more expensive, so practical implementation may require more specialized algorithmic or hardware strategies than the current general approach.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
